course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Cold War and Decolonization
unit.description: Study how the Cold War divided the world, how colonies won independence, how new states and movements challenged established power, and why the Cold War ended.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.5 key concept: some colonies, such as India, achieved independence largely through negotiation and mass nonviolent movements
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing Indian independence, 1942–1947
stimulusBlocks.text:
During World War II, Mohandas Gandhi and the Indian National Congress launched the Quit India Movement in 1942, demanding an immediate end to British rule. The British jailed tens of thousands of its members. After the war, Britain was exhausted and no longer able to hold India by force.

The Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, demanded a separate state for Muslims. In August 1947 British India was divided into two independent countries, India and Pakistan, in negotiations that both nationalist parties joined.

questions.prompt: The Muslim League's demand described in the passage most directly led to

continued British rule over India until 1960
questions.explanation: British India was divided into two countries.
choiceExplanations: British India was divided into two countries.
1942 was the year of Quit India; independence came in 1947.
India and Pakistan became separate states.
Britain left in 1947.
questions.distinguisher: The Quit India campaign began in 1942; independence came in 1947.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.5 key concept: independence came through negotiation in some colonies and through armed struggle in others
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, comparing independence in Ghana and Algeria, 1950–1962
stimulusBlocks.text:
In the British colony of the Gold Coast, Kwame Nkrumah organized strikes and boycotts and won elections under a new constitution. Britain negotiated a gradual transfer of power, and in 1957 the colony became independent Ghana, one of the first African colonies south of the Sahara to win independence.

In Algeria, about one million European settlers lived under French rule, and France treated Algeria as part of France itself. The National Liberation Front began an armed revolt in 1954. The war lasted eight years, both sides committed atrocities, and Algeria won independence in 1962.

questions.prompt: The passage suggests that France fought to keep Algeria because

questions.explanation: Settlers and France's legal claim made Algeria different.
choiceExplanations: The passage does not mention the Soviet bloc.
Ghana was British.
Settlers and France's legal claim made Algeria different.
The National Liberation Front led a revolt.
questions.distinguisher: Algeria had an armed independence movement, which France fought.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.5 key concept: armed independence movements developed where colonial powers or settler populations resisted decolonization
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing armed independence struggles in Vietnam and Kenya, 1945–1963
stimulusBlocks.text:
When France tried to reclaim Indochina after World War II, the Viet Minh under Ho Chi Minh fought back. Their victory at Dien Bien Phu in 1954 ended French rule, though Vietnam was divided into a communist north and an anticommunist south.

In Kenya, Kikuyu farmers who had lost land to white settlers formed the Mau Mau movement and rebelled in 1952. British forces crushed the revolt and detained tens of thousands of Kenyans in camps, but Britain granted Kenya independence in 1963.

questions.distinguisher: Vietnam fought France, but Kenya's rebels fought Britain.

questions.prompt: Which detail best supports the claim that Vietnam's struggle became tied to Cold War rivalry?
choices: Ho Chi Minh's declaration of Vietnamese independence in 1945
American support for a non-communist government in the south
The Viet Minh siege of the French base at Dien Bien Phu
The mix of nationalists and communists within the Viet Minh
questions.explanation: American support for the southern government, motivated by fear of communism, tied the conflict to the global contest between the superpowers.
choiceExplanations: A declaration of independence shows nationalism but not Cold War involvement.
American support for the southern government, motivated by fear of communism, tied the conflict to the global contest between the superpowers.
A siege shows the military struggle against France.
A mixed coalition shows the movement's makeup, but it does not show outside powers' involvement.
questions.distinguisher: The Viet Minh coalition included communists, but the outside involvement that made the war a Cold War conflict was American support for the south.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 8.5 key concept: some independence movements used armed struggle, and Cold War rivalry shaped the outcome
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Vietnamese struggle against French rule, 1945–1954
stimulusBlocks.text:
After World War II, France tried to restore its rule in Indochina. Ho Chi Minh, who had declared Vietnam's independence in 1945, led the Viet Minh, a coalition of nationalists and communists, in a guerrilla war against the French. In 1954 Viet Minh forces under General Vo Nguyen Giap besieged the French base at Dien Bien Phu and forced its surrender.

At the Geneva Conference that followed, the great powers divided Vietnam temporarily at the 17th parallel, with the communists governing the north. The United States, fearing that communism would spread, supported a non-communist government in the south, and the conflict continued.

questions.prompt: Vietnam's path to independence differed from India's primarily because
choices: Vietnam received independence by peaceful agreement, while India had to fight a long war
Vietnam was never colonized by a European power but was ruled only by Japan
Vietnam's independence was won by war, while India's came mainly through nonviolent pressure
India was divided by the great powers at an international conference in Geneva
questions.explanation: The Viet Minh waged guerrilla war and won at Dien Bien Phu, while India's movement under Gandhi and Nehru relied on mass nonviolent protest and talks with Britain.
choiceExplanations: The reverse is true: Vietnam fought and India negotiated.
France ruled Indochina, including Vietnam, for decades.
The Viet Minh waged guerrilla war and won at Dien Bien Phu, while India's movement under Gandhi and Nehru relied on mass nonviolent protest and talks with Britain.
India was partitioned by Britain at independence; the Geneva Conference concerned Vietnam.
questions.distinguisher: Both Vietnam and India were divided as they became independent, but India was partitioned by Britain, not by a great-power conference.

questions.prompt: France's attempt to restore control in Indochina after 1945 is best explained by
choices: a request from the United Nations that France administer the territory
a wish to regain prestige and resources despite wartime weakness
the Atlantic Charter's promise to restore prewar colonial borders

questions.explanation: France had been occupied during the war and sought to restore its empire as part of recovering as a great power.
choiceExplanations: The United Nations did not ask France to resume control.
France had been occupied during the war and sought to restore its empire as part of recovering as a great power.
The Atlantic Charter endorsed self-determination, which nationalists used against colonial rule.
No such vote took place; Ho Chi Minh had declared independence, and France reclaimed Indochina by force.
questions.distinguisher: Japan had indeed controlled Indochina during the war, but its defeat in 1945 ended that control and created the opening France tried to fill.
